transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery and recovery. 

Do you have any questions for me today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi, Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. Firstly, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great! So gardening is considered light exercise, and you can start doing that after 1 week following your surgery.

Just make sure to be careful around water - try to avoid getting water in your eye, especially in that first month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for the advice. I do have another question: when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you're not sure or need clarification on your specific drops, I'd recommend checking with your GP or care team.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the information. I am also very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
Yes, some sensitivity to bright light is quite normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. 

If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check that further. In that case, do let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the tip! Lastly, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long ago was your surgery? That would help me give you better guidance on whether what you're experiencing is normal.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: My surgery was about a week ago.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's helpful to know. Since it's been about a week, some blurriness at this stage is quite normal and should improve over the coming days and weeks.

However, if your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I think that covers everything. Thank you for the information!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Brilliant! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you've answered all my questions. Thanks again for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and best of luck with your recovery.
